sections.title: Three singular pronouns
sections.content: Hungarian uses én for I, te for you and ő for both he and she.

Hungarian will happily drop these pronouns later once the verb ending already makes the subject clear — Károly vagyok already means "I am Károly" with no én in sight. The explicit én/te/ő you're drilling now are mostly for emphasis or contrast. Spanish and Italian speakers will recognise the trick immediately (they drop yo/tú the same way); English just never learned to let go.
